selectionReason: RC56 stopped at two explicit prerequisites: unresolved Aurora cohort lineage and an insufficient endpoint-pair budget. RC57 tested those prerequisites without opening target outcomes and added autonomous laboratories because experiment scheduling and provenance are causal parts of the measurement, not administrative details.
newFacts: The Aurora RO-Crate contains 599 graph entities: one metadata descriptor, one root dataset, 199 cell datasets, and 398 BDF file entities. It inventories all 199 physical cell directories consistently.

The RO-Crate contains no chemistry, Figure 7, or 36-cell study-cohort relation. It therefore cannot reconcile the paper's 36-cell LFP batch with the 32 per-cell metadata records that explicitly identify LiFePO4.
This absence is not called an RO-Crate conformance failure because the specification permits metadata to describe some or all payload files; it is a fitness-for-selection failure for this study.
Twelve four-cell RWTH blocks have a hard maximum of 72 within-block pairs. No denser RPT schedule can reach the registered 100-pair target while preserving those blocks.
An exact multinomial calculation resampled 48 interpolated design-proxy crossings, compressed lifetime spread to 100%, 75%, 50%, and 25%, and exhausted every integer phase of seven endpoint grids.

With 24 usable observed events and quarter-width lifetime spread, the largest registered interval passing worst-phase P(pair>=100)>=0.95 and a lower 5% pair count >=100 was 25 cycles: P=0.999357 and lower 5% count=150.
With 36 usable events under the same conservative scenario, 50 cycles passed: P=0.993685 and lower 5% count=159. The lower-burden branch therefore depends on retaining all 36 events.
Python and dependency-free Node implementations matched all 56 design rows, selected intervals, integer quantiles, and gate decisions; their largest probability difference was 3.33e-16.
Aurora remains excluded and zero BDF cycling entries, cell capacities, or EOL values were opened.

H57-0.claim: The public Aurora package identifies all 36 Figure 7 LFP cells without outcome access.
H57-0.prediction: The RO-Crate or per-cell metadata contains one explicit 36-member study relation with unique metadata and BDF links.
H57-0.decisiveTest: Parse the remote central directory and RO-Crate graph and join it to the sealed RC56 metadata audit.
H57-0.reason: The inventory is internally complete for 199 cells but has no study-cohort relation, and only 32 records explicitly state LiFePO4.

H57-1.claim: Increasing endpoint measurement frequency alone can repair the RC56 pair deficit in the existing four-cell blocks.
H57-1.prediction: At least one grid produces 100 within-block non-tied pairs.
H57-1.decisiveTest: Calculate the block-combinatorial ceiling before simulating cadence.

H57-2.claim: One larger same-condition block can meet the pair gate with a fixed endpoint register despite a much narrower lifetime distribution and adverse grid alignment.
H57-2.prediction: A registered interval retains exact worst-phase probability at least 0.95 and a lower 5% pair count at least 100 after quarter-spread compression.
H57-2.decisiveTest: Evaluate the exact multinomial distribution for all registered event counts, spreads, intervals, and integer phases.
H57-2.result: 25 cycles for 24 events; 50 cycles for 36 events. This is design evidence, not feature validation.

H57-3.claim: A capacity-loss-triggered endpoint register can reduce RPT burden without changing the degradation process or coupling feature and endpoint.
H57-3.prediction: A separate pilot meets a predefined degradation-equivalence margin while triggering before the 80% endpoint with high sensitivity.
H57-3.decisiveTest: Randomize a non-confirmatory pilot between fixed and triggered schedules using identical stress and calibrated channels.
H57-3.reason: Published condition-based RPT results establish feasibility and test-time savings, not equivalence for this coordinate or cohort.

causalChainOutcome.fastFailureEvidence: Four cells provide six pairs per block and twelve blocks provide at most 72.

causalChainOutcome.fastFailureEvidence: Exact worst-phase distributions distinguish a 25-cycle 24-event default from a conditional 50-cycle 36-event branch.

causalChainOutcome.fastFailureEvidence: No manifest-qualified target or schedule-equivalence pilot exists, so target outcomes remain closed.

minimalAcademicAdvance: The failed pair gate is now localized to experimental block geometry rather than feature weakness or cadence alone. The project also distinguishes a standards-compliant data package from a package sufficiently expressive for outcome-blind cohort selection.

mostPromisingNextPath.hypothesis: A fixed R3 capacity coordinate can receive a fair independent ordinal test when a 36-cell same-condition block has explicit specimen lineage and an endpoint register designed against narrow lifetime spread and unfavorable grid alignment.
mostPromisingNextPath.differentCombination: Use two measurement registers: sparse fixed checks through the cycle-480 feature landmark and a separate 25-cycle endpoint register thereafter. Combine this with exact block-level pair power, channel randomization, and a paper-to-file cohort manifest.
mostPromisingNextPath.exactBottleneck: No current public target jointly satisfies exact cohort lineage, sufficient within-condition block size, and demonstrated non-interference of the endpoint schedule.
mostPromisingNextPath.firstDecisiveAction: Metadata-screen alternative public cohorts without opening outcomes. Admit only a source with at least 36 same-condition cells and an explicit specimen-protocol-file manifest; otherwise publish a prospective acquisition preregistration rather than reusing Aurora.
mostPromisingNextPath.successSignal: A sealed target manifest plus a schedule-equivalence pilot and an exact design with at least 24 events, at least 100 non-tied pairs, and no outcome-dependent changes.
mostPromisingNextPath.rejectionAndStop: Exclude any archive whose cohort requires inferred IDs. If dense RPTs fail equivalence or no manifest-qualified block exists, stop capacity-only confirmation and move to a repeatability-qualified orthogonal observable.
mostPromisingNextPath.failureValue: A negative screen tells the platform whether the missing resource is provenance, experimental scale, or a less invasive sensor rather than another prediction model.

workPackages.failNext: Exclude the source; do not infer or inspect outcomes.

workPackages.method: Freeze BOL/160/320/480 checks for the candidate and a 25-cycle post-480 endpoint grid.
workPackages.pass: The endpoint register cannot alter or recompute the feature coordinate.
workPackages.failNext: Redesign before any target cell is tested.

workPackages.output: Equivalence interval for life, temperature, throughput, and impedance change.
workPackages.pass: Every predefined intervention metric remains within its scientific equivalence margin.
workPackages.failNext: Reject the fixed dense schedule and test a frozen condition-triggered or orthogonal-sensor branch.

workPackages.method: Open target outcomes only after W57-1 through W57-3 pass; compute the sealed coordinate and blocked concordance in two implementations.
workPackages.output: Coverage, events, pair count, C, bootstrap lower bound, calibration boundary, and immutable decision.
workPackages.pass: Coverage>=90%, events>=24, pairs>=100, C>=0.65, lower 95% bound>0.50, and implementation agreement.
workPackages.failNext: Reject capacity-only transport; preserve the result as a boundary for the orthogonal-sensor branch.

failedAttempts: The Aurora RO-Crate did not resolve the four-cell difference; Aurora was excluded without opening BDF outcomes.
Cadence-only repair of the original four-cell blocks is mathematically impossible because their pair ceiling is 72.
A 50-cycle schedule is not conservative when only 24 events are usable under quarter-spread and worst-phase analysis; the passing default tightens to 25 cycles.
Condition-based RPT remains a burden-reduction hypothesis because intervention equivalence is not established by the available paper.
unverifiedClaims: The identities and disposition of the four Aurora paper-cohort cells absent from explicit LFP metadata remain unknown.
The quarter-spread sensitivity scenario may still be wider than a highly uniform automated batch.
A 25-cycle RPT schedule may alter degradation enough to invalidate passive-observation assumptions.
R3 normalized capacity level has not been tested in any untouched target cohort.
safetyEthics: Only public metadata and previously opened historical RWTH trajectories were processed. No target cycling outcome, physical cell, personal data, cyber experiment, safety decision, or deployment was accessed. A future physical protocol requires laboratory electrical, chemical, thermal, and emergency controls.
nextCycleStart: Outcome-blind metadata-screen candidate public cohorts for an explicit same-condition block of at least 36 cells. If one qualifies, freeze its IDs and run a schedule-intervention audit before outcomes. If none qualifies, create a prospective acquisition preregistration and begin the orthogonal-sensor evidence screen rather than reopening Aurora.
